title: People review a Change at two gates, and nothing stops between them
context: Split out of ADR-0045. Each Change used to keep four pages and a lifecycle file, all committed and reconciled at Archive. On team-membership-authorization, 24 of 50 commits touched only Blueprint, 13 of them resynchronising pages after a gate, and the developer answered 28 gate prompts.
decision: A person reviews a Change twice: G1 before Apply and G2 before the pull request opens. Everything between the two gates runs unattended. What each gate accepts is recorded in ADR-0060.

alternatives.option: Keep the four pages but trim their sections
alternatives.reason: The cost came from how often the pages had to be rewritten and reconciled, not from their length; trimming leaves every per-round and Archive obligation in place.

consequences: Questions that arise between gates wait for the next gate unless a different answer would make the remaining work useless.
